name: Chilisso
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Only sociolinguistic survey material (Hallberg 1992, SSNP; Rensch wordlists, Biddulph 1880); no grammar or phonology of Chilisso exists per Glottolog.

sources.citation: Murad, Amna. 2025. Chilisso Dictionary (5-page draft wordlist, archive.org, uploaded 2025-06-29).
sources.note: No front matter; entries mark vowel length and nasality only, no stress or tone.

sources.citation: Murad, Amna & Baber Sultan Ali Khan. 2026. Language vitality of Chilisso: a case of an endangered language of Pakistan. UCP Journal of Languages & Literature 4(1): 90-118. doi:10.24312/ucp-jll.04.01.945 (CC BY).
sources.note: Silent (sociolinguistic survey). Its literature review names only Biddulph 1880, Hallberg 1992 and Liljegren & Akhunzada 2017 as prior work and calls Chilisso 'undocumented'.

sources.citation: Liljegren, Henrik & Fakhruddin Akhunzada. 2017. Linguistic diversity, vitality and maintenance: a case study on the language situation in northern Pakistan. Multiethnica 36-37: 61-79.
sources.note: Cited by Murad & Khan 2026 as one of only three prior works on Chilisso; sociolinguistic, unlikely but not verified to contain a phonological note.

sources.citation: Liljegren, Henrik. 2017. Profiling Indo-Aryan in the Hindukush-Karakoram. JSALL 4(1), Table 2 data sources.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Chilisso coded from Hallberg 1992 only, no own data; hence no first-hand Chilisso tone/accent value in its sec. 4.8.

sources.citation: Baart, Joan L.G. 2003. Tonal features in languages of northern Pakistan. In Baart & Sindhi (eds.), Pakistani languages and society, 132-144. Islamabad: NIPS & SIL (FLI offprint pagination).
sources.note: Table 1 (offprint pp. 2-3) lists 'Chilisso Yes?' for tonal status; Table 3 (p. 6) puts 'Chilisso?' under the Shina-type (lexical stress on one mora with H tone) with a question mark. Explicitly a guess, no Chilisso data.

sources.citation: Hallberg, Daniel G. 1992. The languages of Indus Kohistan, ch. 3 'Chilisso' pp. 116-123; App. D.1 Indus Kohistan word lists pp. 207-225 (CHM Mahrin, CHJ Jalkot); App. D.2.4 Chilisso story pp. 240-243. In Rensch, Decker & Hallberg, Languages of Kohistan (SSNP 1). Islamabad: NIPS & SIL.
sources.note: Silent on any rule. Chapter is sociolinguistic (lexical similarity, RTT, bilingualism). Field wordlists mark stress with a prime on 85 of 136 Chilisso rows in varying positions (su'ràt, 'nothu0, hà'gwi, hàlà'li, sVT'ko, 'cubV); p. 146 warns transcriptions 'have not undergone thorough phonological and grammatical analysis'; the story text has no stress marks.

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. 1919. Linguistic Survey of India VIII.2 (Dardic), Kohistani section: Torwali pp. 514ff. with Chilis account; Maiya sketch with a 'Chilis' column in the List of Standard Words (from Biddulph).
sources.note: Silent; Chilis appears only as ethnographic paragraph and Biddulph's wordlist column.

sources.citation: Biddulph, John. 1880. Tribes of the Hindoo Koosh. Calcutta: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing. Appendix: short grammar of 'Chiliss' (pp. lxvii ff.) and comparative vocabulary.
sources.note: Silent. The Explanatory Note's accents are vowel-quality marks ('a unaccented.. as in have; á.. as the short a in America'), not stress; nothing on accent in the Chiliss sketch.

sources.citation: ELAR deposit 'Preserving Chilisso: Documentation of Oral Heritage', depositors Amna Murad & Jahan Zaib, status Forthcoming.
sources.note: Catalogue page lists no written description yet (one JPEG placeholder).
